approval_required_for: installing a dependency, skill, plugin, MCP server, CLI, or service
copying source code or substantial documentation
rules: Public visibility is not a licence.
Verify the licence at the exact tag or commit before reuse.
Inspect hooks, scripts, permissions, MCP tools, and network access.
Do not combine overlapping harness installations without an explicit decision.

resources.name: awesome-design-md
resources.use_when: A product needs a design archetype, component language, visual benchmark, or product-specific DESIGN.md.
resources.how_to_use: Read only the relevant company DESIGN.md files, extract principles, and create an original system under client-brand precedence.
resources.do_not: Do not copy protected logos, proprietary fonts, imagery, screenshots, or another company's trade dress.
resources.escapement_inspiration: The 73-company design-intelligence synthesis and design-system routing.

resources.name: Perplexity AI GitHub organisation
resources.use_when: An agent needs current patterns for research tooling, evaluation runners, safe binary distribution, or developer-tool inventory.
resources.how_to_use: Select a specific repository from this catalogue and verify its current licence before reuse.
resources.do_not: Do not assume every public repository in an organisation has the same licence.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Research extension, resumable evals, content-addressed records, self-tests, and safe installers.

resources.name: api-platform-developers
resources.use_when: The project needs official Perplexity Agent Skills, a Claude/Codex plugin example, or live documentation through MCP.
resources.how_to_use: Prefer installing the official skill/plugin or using it as the model for portable Agent Skills. Pin a release or commit.
resources.do_not: Do not make Perplexity credentials or the docs MCP mandatory for Escapement core.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Portable skills, plugin manifests, optional docs MCP, and an official research extension.

resources.name: pplx CLI
resources.license: No licence file observed during review
resources.use_when: A user explicitly wants Perplexity-backed current web search or snippets and can provide an API key.
resources.how_to_use: Use the released CLI as an optional external dependency after approval. Verify checksum and current terms.
resources.do_not: Do not copy repository code into Escapement or claim open-source reuse until a licence is present and verified.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Checksum-verified releases, atomic updates, JSON stdout, and agent-friendly CLI design.

resources.name: search_evals
resources.use_when: Escapement needs reproducible eval suites, provider adapters, task traces, resumable runs, or cost/evidence accounting.
resources.how_to_use: Adapt the run-directory, config-hash, resume, trace, and summary patterns to local harness evaluations.
resources.do_not: Do not import paid-provider assumptions or third-party benchmark data without accepting their separate terms.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Resumable executable evaluations and inspectable per-task traces.

resources.name: Bumblebee
resources.use_when: A security review needs read-only package, skill, editor-extension, or MCP inventory from local metadata.
resources.how_to_use: Prefer invoking Bumblebee externally. Reuse its read-only, profile-based, NDJSON, confidence, and self-test patterns where useful.
resources.do_not: Do not expose credentials found in MCP env blocks or broaden scans beyond approved roots.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Read-only inventory profiles, structured NDJSON, confidence levels, and built-in self-test.

resources.name: Perplexity MCP server
resources.use_when: A project wants Perplexity search through MCP rather than a CLI.
resources.how_to_use: Install as an optional project MCP after explicit approval, review its tools, permissions, network access, and credential storage.
resources.do_not: Do not register remote MCP servers silently or make network access part of the default core.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Optional freshness and research integrations through a narrow MCP boundary.

resources.name: Codescythe
resources.use_when: A TypeScript or JavaScript repository needs deterministic dead-code analysis or dependency-path explanation.
resources.how_to_use: Use as an external check after approval. Run doctor/explain before destructive fix mode and capture output through structured evidence.
resources.do_not: Do not run destructive fixes without a clean branch, tests, and explicit approval.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Narrow deterministic contracts, doctor commands, explainability, and safe destructive-mode gates.

resources.name: AppFlowy
resources.use_when: Designing local-first state, user-owned data, extensible workspace architecture, or self-hosted collaboration.
resources.how_to_use: Reuse architectural principles or integrate as a separate service under its licence. Review AGPL obligations before copying code.
resources.do_not: Do not copy AGPL code into Escapement's source-available core without a deliberate licence decision.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Privacy-first local control, cross-platform reliability, and extensible building blocks.

resources.name: Plausible Analytics
resources.use_when: Designing privacy-first observability, minimal dashboards, transparent metrics, or optional self-hosted analytics.
resources.how_to_use: Adopt privacy and simplicity principles or integrate a separately deployed instance under its licence.
resources.do_not: Do not embed AGPL application code into Escapement core without licence review.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Local-only telemetry by default, transparent metrics, and clutter-free observability.

resources.name: Spec Kit
resources.use_when: New or material work needs a constitution, executable specification, technical plan, task breakdown, or convergence review.
resources.how_to_use: Use Spec Kit directly or adapt its phases and extension/preset/bundle model with attribution.
resources.do_not: Do not duplicate its whole command surface in Escapement when an optional integration is sufficient.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Constitution → specify → plan → tasks → implement → converge, plus extensions, presets, and bundles.

resources.name: 500+ AI Agent Projects & Use Cases
resources.use_when: An agent needs to discover relevant implementation patterns or comparable industry use cases.
resources.how_to_use: Search the catalogue, inspect the linked source project, and independently verify that project's licence and quality.
resources.do_not: Do not treat inclusion in a catalogue as proof of safety, quality, maintenance, or licence compatibility.
resources.escapement_inspiration: A curated agent-pattern registry rather than hundreds of always-loaded agents.

resources.name: Learn Harness Engineering
resources.use_when: Creating, assessing, or teaching the instructions, tools, environment, state, and feedback subsystems of a harness.
resources.how_to_use: Use relevant lectures, templates, and projects; compare weak and strong harness outcomes; preserve attribution.
resources.do_not: Do not load the complete course into every task or confuse a prompt file with a complete harness.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Repository as system of record, feature-state primitives, lifecycle bootstrap, verification, and clean session closure.

resources.name: harness-creator skill
resources.use_when: A project lacks a harness or needs a structured five-subsystem assessment.
resources.how_to_use: Install through the skills ecosystem or reference its SKILL.md; run its evaluations before adopting changes.
resources.do_not: Do not install it on top of overlapping native Escapement harness skills without an overlap decision.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Harness assessment, templates, reference patterns, and benchmark-oriented skill development.

resources.name: Penpot
resources.use_when: A product needs open design tokens, inspectable design-to-code workflows, or an optional design MCP/API.
resources.how_to_use: Prefer integration through its API/MCP or adopt open-standard design-token concepts. Review MPL file-level obligations before code reuse.
resources.do_not: Do not copy branding or assume a design file alone proves implementation correctness.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Design tokens as shared source of truth and programmable design-code integration.

resources.name: HelixDB
resources.use_when: A project genuinely needs graph-vector memory, knowledge graphs, or a local agent data layer.
resources.how_to_use: Integrate as an optional data service after architecture approval; adapt its one-shot bootstrap and explainable local setup patterns.
resources.do_not: Do not make a database mandatory for Escapement's file-based core or add it merely to appear agentic.
resources.escapement_inspiration: A guided one-shot bootstrap and optional structured memory backend.

resources.name: Agent Reach
resources.use_when: A user explicitly needs internet/platform access not already available through approved tools.
resources.how_to_use: Use its safe mode, local credential model, doctor, and primary/fallback provider approach after reviewing every installed tool.
resources.do_not: Do not bypass platform protections, harvest credentials, or install broad internet capabilities without explicit approval.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Capability doctor, safe mode, fallback routing, and agent-friendly configuration.

resources.name: agent-browser
resources.use_when: A frontend or end-to-end task needs real browser evidence, accessibility-tree interaction, screenshots, or DOM inspection.
resources.how_to_use: Install as an optional external CLI, pin its version, restrict allowed domains, and capture commands/screenshots as evidence.
resources.do_not: Do not browse authenticated or sensitive sites without approval or use browser automation as proof when business data is fabricated.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Agent-readable accessibility snapshots, early interaction failure, and browser-based verification.

resources.name: GSD Core
resources.use_when: A project needs phase-level context isolation, fresh execution contexts, or a discuss-plan-execute-verify-ship loop.
resources.how_to_use: Integrate directly or adopt focused context-isolation and phase-verification patterns.
resources.do_not: Do not run parallel agents when tasks share mutable state or when the repository lacks merge and verification controls.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Fresh-context phase execution, lean main sessions, and verified shipping.

resources.name: mcp-builder skill
resources.use_when: A project is approved to build an MCP server for an external API or service.
resources.how_to_use: Install or read the skill; research the current MCP specification; design concise tools, schemas, annotations, errors, pagination, and evaluations.
resources.do_not: Do not expose broad destructive endpoints, secrets, or an unbounded API surface to agents.
resources.escapement_inspiration: MCP quality workflow, tool discoverability, output schemas, annotations, and realistic evaluations.

resources.name: find-skills skill
resources.use_when: A task requires a specialised capability that Escapement core does not own.
resources.how_to_use: Search the skills ecosystem, check source reputation and maintenance, inspect the skill, verify its licence, then request installation approval.
resources.do_not: Do not recommend or install a skill solely because it ranks highly or has many installs.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Reference-router skill and a quality gate before external skill installation.

resources.name: ECC
resources.use_when: Reviewing cross-runtime distribution, doctor/repair, installation conflict detection, skill packaging, or harness security.
resources.how_to_use: Study or integrate narrowly selected capabilities; avoid overlapping full installations in the same agent runtime.
resources.do_not: Do not copy its hundreds of agents/skills into Escapement core or imply full platform parity.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Doctor/repair, official-source warning, install-conflict prevention, security scanning, and support matrix honesty.

resources.name: Strix
resources.use_when: The user has explicit authorisation to dynamically assess a local, owned, or approved target in a sandbox.
resources.how_to_use: Run as an external optional tool with a written scope, exclusions, credentials policy, target approval, and structured evidence.
resources.do_not: Do not autonomously attack public or third-party targets, run exploits without permission, or place offensive capability in Escapement core.
resources.escapement_inspiration: Local run viewer, evidence-rich findings, CI security gates, and sandboxed external security integrations.
